instrucciones: For questions 9–16, read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap.
texto:
When a group of neighbours first proposed turning a derelict car park into a community garden, few people believed it {{9}} ever happen. The land had been abandoned for years, and the council, {{10}} was short of money, showed little interest. Undeterred, the volunteers began clearing rubbish at weekends, {{11}} only a few borrowed spades and a great deal of enthusiasm.

It was not long {{12}} the project began to attract attention. A local builder donated timber for raised beds, and a nearby school asked whether its pupils could take {{13}} in the planting. By the end of the first summer, the garden was producing more vegetables than the volunteers knew what to do {{14}}, so they began leaving surplus crates at the gate for anyone who wanted them.

No sooner {{15}} the first harvest been shared than people started asking how they could get involved. Today, the garden is run by more than eighty residents, many of {{16}} had never grown anything before.

items.explicacion: "Believed it would ever happen" is reported speech about the future seen from the past, so "would" is needed.
A non-defining relative clause ("the council, which was short of money") needs "which"; "that" cannot follow a comma.
"With only a few borrowed spades" = using or having only those tools. "Armed with" would need two words.
"It was not long before..." is a fixed expression meaning that something happened soon.
"Take part in" = participate in. It is a fixed expression.
"Knew what to do with" = how to deal with. The verb "do" takes the preposition "with" here.
After "No sooner" we use inversion with the past perfect: "No sooner had the harvest been shared than...".
After a quantifier and preposition ("many of whom"), the relative pronoun must be "whom" for people.
